items.question: Why does DeepWalk use weighted edges and matrix factorization to capture first-order proximity on citation networks like DBLP(PaperCitation)?
items.false_premise: DeepWalk uses weighted edges, matrix factorization, and first-order proximity, and it applies to citation networks like DBLP(PaperCitation).
items.correction: DeepWalk is only applicable for networks with binary edges, and only second-order proximity is utilized through truncated random walks.
items.evidence_quote: DeepWalk is an approach recently proposed for social network embedding, which is only applicable for networks with binary edges.

items.question: How does graph factorization extend to directed networks such as DBLP(PaperCitation) while optimizing its embedding objective with random walks?
items.false_premise: Graph factorization extends to directed networks and uses random walks to optimize its embedding objective.
items.correction: Graph factorization is optimized through stochastic gradient descent, and it only applies to undirected networks.
items.evidence_quote: Graph factorization is optimized through stochastic gradient descent and is able to handle large networks.

items.question: Under which conditions does LINE-SGD treat sampled edges as binary and use edge-sampling instead of direct gradient updates?
items.false_premise: LINE-SGD uses edge-sampling treatment and treats sampled edges as binary instead of using direct gradient updates.
items.correction: LINE-SGD optimizes the objective Eqn. (3) or Eqn. (6) directly with stochastic gradient descent, and the weights of the edges are directly multiplied into the gradients when the edges are sampled for model updating.
items.evidence_quote: LINE-SGD. This is the LINE model introduced in Section 4.1 that optimizes the objective Eqn. (3) or Eqn. (6) directly with stochastic gradient descent.

items.question: What explains why LINE(1st) and LINE-SGD(1st) are designed for directed graphs rather than undirected graphs?
items.false_premise: LINE(1st) and LINE-SGD(1st) are designed for directed graphs.
items.correction: Both LINE(1st) and LINE-SGD(1st) only apply to undirected graphs.
items.evidence_quote: Like the graph factorization, both LINE(1st) and LINE-SGD(1st) only apply to undirected graphs.
